sentences.text: This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.50/2019 dated 07.12.2019 registered at Police Station E.O.W. District Bhopal for the offences punishable under Sections 420 read with Section 120-B of the IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the present applicant as well as co-accused Sachin Upadhyay had filed a bail application for anticipatory bail before this Court vide M.Cr.C.
No.4671/2024.
This Court dismissed the said application vide order dated 27.02.2024.

It is contended by the counsel that this Court while dismissing the application for grant of anticipatory bail filed by the present applicant and Sachin Upadhyay, proceeded on an assumption that against the present applicant also a case under Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act was registered.

It is contended by the counsel that so far as present applicant is concerned, against Ashish Upadhyay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94392571/
1 him no case under Sections 13(1)(B) or 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act was registered.

entities.text: Ashish Upadhyay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case under the aforesaid section was registered against co- accused Sachin Upadhyay.

The counsel contends that though in paragraph 8 of the order, this Court has observed this fact that the case under Sections 13(1) (B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act was registered against Shri Suresh Upadhyay, Smt. Anuradha Upadhyay and Sachin Upadhyay but, in subsequent paragraph i.e. paragraphs 12 and 14 of the order, this Court observed that the aforesaid case was also registered against the present applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that it escaped the attention of this Court that no case under the provisions of Prevention of Corruption Act was ever registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that against the present applicant neither any case was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act nor any order of attachment was passed.

It is also contended by the counsel that there was a bonafide mistake while executing the sale-deed in favour of Beer Bahadur Singh as plot no.181 which was situated on Khasra no.422 was not to be alienated, on the contrary, plot no.213 which was part of Khasra no.422 was to be sold.

Thus,
immediately a suit was filed, which has also been decreed.

It is also contended by the counsel that the purchaser expressed his no objection regarding prayer made in the suit and accordingly,
considering the no objection of the purchaser, the suit has been decreed and the sale deed made in favour of Shri Beer Bhadur Singh has been declared as null and void.

4. It is also contended by the counsel that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51 and also in the case o f Mahdoom Bava vs. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 218, there is no need to arrest the applicant and no custodial interrogation was required.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant further contends that while proceeding against the co-accused and two other persons namely Suresh Upadhyay and Smt. Anuradha Upadhyay, the prosecution after investigation had exonerated the applicant which is evident from charge-sheet in respect of offence registered under Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
The charge-sheet itself reflects that no involvement of the present applicant was found.
The present applicant is nephew of Shri Suresh Upadhyay who is one of the accused in the case filed under Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
It is thus, contended by the counsel that there was an inadvertent lapse which was rectified by the Civil Court while passing judgement and decree.
There was no mens rea so far as the present applicant is concerned nor any order of attachment was in respect of the property which was sought to be alienated to Beer Bhadur Singh.

Hence the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that even the subsequent bail application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. can be entertained and in support of the said contention, the counsel for the applicant has reliance on the order passed by this Court in the case of Khalik vs. The State of M.P. (M.Cr.C. No.37693/2022) and in the case of Balendra Shekhar vs. The State of M.P. (M.Cr.C.
No.13543/2022).

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and submitted that the present application which has been filed under the grab of review petition deserves to be dismissed.
This Court recently while dealing with the application filed by the present applicant for grant of anticipatory bail, dismissed the same vide order dated 27.02.2024.

It is contended by the counsel that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Hari Singh Mann vs. Harbhajan Singh Bajwa an Ors. (2001 1 SCC 169), the application for grant of anticipatory bail deserves to be dismissed.

sentences.text:
8. It is also contended by the counsel that paragraph 8 of the rejection order passed in M.Cr.C.
No.4671/2024 dated 27.02.2024 reveals that this Court was conscious of the fact that the present applicant was not an accused in the case which was filed vide Crime No.25/2019 under Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

It is contended by the counsel that though in paragraphs 12 and 14, it is mentioned that the case against the applicants was registered under the provision of Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act but the said observations are immaterial in view of paragraph 8 of the order.
Thus, counsel submits that the application deserves to be dismissed.

9. Heard the submissions and perused the record.
10.

The applicant despite rejection of first application for anticipatory bail recently on 27.02.2024,
again has filed this application.

The applicants stand that earlier application was dismissed by this Court while observing that the present applicant was also one of the accused in the case filed vide Crime No.25/2019 under Sections 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

11. So far as the applicant being an accused in the case filed vide Crime No.25/2019 under the provision of Prevention of Corruption Act is concerned, it is undisputed that the present applicant is not an accused.
The allegations against the applicant that he alienated the property i.e. plot no.181 situated on Khasra No.422 Mauja Kajarwara.

After execution of sale-deed, the purchaser Beer Bahadur Singh, reported the matter to the police and in which, he complained that the said plot was sold to him without informing him that the property, which he was going to purchase, was under attachment.

In the statement, Beer Bahadur Singh says that he was shown various plots by the present applicant as well as co-accused Sachin Upadhyay and one of the plot i.e. plat No.181 was choosen by the purchaser and accordingly, the amount of consideration was paid and sale-deed was also registered.
In the said sale-deed, vendor is the present applicant and as per the statement of Beer Bahadur Singh, the amount of consideration was transferred in the account of co-accused Sachin Upadhyay.

12. The record produced by the prosecution further reflects that pertaining to case registered vide Crime No.25/2019, on 25.06.2019, a search of the house of the applicant was also carried out though nothing incriminating was found against the present applicant in that case.
Thus, the factum of registration of the said case vide Crime No.25/2019 and ensued investigation was within the knowledge of the present applicant.

This Court while dismissing the previous application has clearly observed in paragraph 10 that the applicant was required to demonstrate that as to whether any plot no.181 existed on Khasra no.422 Mauja Kajarwara, Settlement no.505, P.C. no.10 Chatanya City,

3 Jabalpur or not.
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court also observed that so far as Khasra no.422 is concerned, there is not a single document on record to demonstrate that there was any division of plot on that Khasra number.

It is also important to take note of the judgment and decree passed in favour of the present applicant which reflects that the present applicant has filed the suit for declaring the sale-deed executed in favour of Beer Bahadur Singh to be null and void on the ground that he intended to alienate some other plot i.e. plot no.213 but not plot no.181.
The sale-deed in favour of Beer Bahadur Singh was executed on 21.10.2019 and suit was filed on 25.11.2019.
14. Therefore, considering the entire record, this Court is of the considered view that the present applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
15. Resultantly, this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. stands dismissed.
16. However, if the applicant surrenders before the trial Court and apply for regular bail, the same shall be dealt with by the trial Court as expeditiously as possible preferably on the same day.
